transcript: A cast chock-full of nepo babies is currently performing a new version of Ghosts at Lincoln Center. This is an Ibsen play from the 1800s about five people all grappling with various concerns under the realm of morality, expectations, and secrets. It has a fair share of revelations and moral quandaries, but I don't know if I'd say it's a “moral thriller” like how it's marketed. The plot is definitely captivating and I think the ideas and themes are basic enough that they'll never not be relevant, but this story and these specific characters felt distant to me, despite the succinct and modernized text by Mark O’Rowe. I was interested enough but I didn't feel anything, which isn't something that really bothered me, just something I noticed. Maybe it was the hit-or-miss direction or the somewhat uneven performances that kept some emotional heights out of reach, but I still enjoyed the story for what it was. And regardless, with names like Hamish Linklater, Billy Crudup, Ella Beatty, Levon Hawke and standout Lily Rabe, I doubt ticket buyers will be deterred by any shortcomings of this particular play or production. And you know what? Good for them. Seats sold are better than seats unsold. With that, another playbill for my collection.
